en.title: Netflix Drops Early 2026 Halloween Horror Slate: Lizzie Borden Returns
en.summary: Spooky season is officially upon us, and Netflix is already teasing its 2026 "Netflix and Chills" lineup. Get ready for a deep dive into true crime and supernatural scares.
en.body:
As the leaves begin to turn and the air grows crisp, Netflix is already preparing to unleash its 2026 "Netflix and Chills" lineup, offering a tantalizing first glimpse into the horror and suspense that awaits us. While the full slate will undoubtedly expand in the coming months, early announcements point towards a blend of returning favorites and chilling new narratives.

## Ryan Murphy Tackles Lizzie Borden in New Series

Leading the charge is **Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story**, set to premiere on September 17th. This limited series marks the return of Ryan Murphy's acclaimed true-crime anthology, this time focusing on one of America's most infamous historical murders. Fans can expect Murphy's signature stylish, bloody, and deeply unsettling approach to unraveling the dark tale of Lizzie Borden. Following closely, on September 24th, is **Balaraw: Blood Island**, a brand-new Filipino horror-thriller. This series promises a potent mix of dark folklore and deadly secrets set against the backdrop of a remote, inescapable island, hinting at a truly claustrophobic and terrifying experience.

## International Scares and Supernatural Workplace Woes

Netflix isn't solely relying on domestic productions. The global reach of the streamer is evident with titles like **Dead-End Job**, a dark Korean fantasy-horror premiering in October. The premise follows a desperate man who accepts a suspiciously high-paying gig, only to find himself trapped in a hellish, supernatural workplace. Adding to the animated horror offerings, **Haunted Hotel** returns for its second season, with the creative force behind *Rick and Morty* bringing back his Halloween-themed adult animation. For those who enjoy a bit of culinary suspense, **Is It Cake? Halloween** also returns for a second season, where bakers will craft holiday-themed cakes to challenge contestants.

## What This Means for Horror Fans

This early reveal suggests Netflix is doubling down on its commitment to horror throughout the year, not just for October. The inclusion of a true-crime deep dive like **Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story** alongside international genre fare and adult animation indicates a broad appeal, aiming to satisfy a wide spectrum of horror aficionados. The strategic placement of these titles, starting in mid-September and extending into November, ensures a sustained period of frights and thrills for binge-watchers and casual viewers alike. The anticipation for these new series, particularly the return of **Monster** and the debut of **Blood Island**, is palpable among genre fans eager for fresh scares.

## What's Next

Mark your calendars for **Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story** on September 17th and **Balaraw: Blood Island** on September 24th. More titles are expected to be announced as we approach the official "Netflix and Chills" season, so keep an eye on the platform for further horror additions.
